result.title: Towards Robust Long-Lived Agents: Benchmarking Experience Lifecycles in Evolving Environments
result.summary: As agents become more capable, they are moving beyond one-off tasks toward sustained assistance across successive user goals. Such assistance requires agents to discover how unfamiliar environments work, reuse what they learn across tasks, and keep that experience current as environments evolve. Existing benchmarks increasingly study experience reuse and adaptation, but provide limited insight into which parts of accumulated experience agents revise, retain, or lose. To address this gap, we introduce ReScopeBench, a benchmark for the experience lifecycle across 18 interactive environments. It distinguishes structural experience about how an environment is organized and accessed from rule experience about reusable principles and constraints that guide decisions across tasks. To study how experience is acquired, reused, and revised, we propose an experience-first construction approach. It builds task streams around shared experience and introduces silent environmental changes. We evaluate task performance and track changes in saved experience throughout each stream. Across 20 models, we find that retained experience improves task performance, but agents struggle to keep it current as environments change. Even when the required experience is correctly recorded, agents do not always complete tasks successfully. These findings identify selective maintenance and effective use as complementary challenges for long-lived agents.

AI.brief_summary: 该文提出 ReScopeBench，覆盖 18 个交互环境，把经验分为结构经验与规则经验，并设计以经验为中心的任务流与环境静默变化，在 20 个模型上同时考察任务表现和已存经验的保留、修订与丢失。
AI.relevance_reason: 虽为非视觉 agent 记忆基准，但其「经验是否被保留、是否被有效使用、环境变化下是否过时」的诊断方式，可能为 LVR 中 latent 状态的信息保存与答案是否真正使用内部内容提供评价思路。
